c-hillsborough|2026-08-05|c09b5d96|5dfdf.title: Human Resources A-45 Approve and execute the Third Modification to the existing Agreement with Humana Insurance Company, (RFP No.8300-3), for fully insured vision benefits for employees and retirees. This modification will extend the contract for three (3) years from January 1, 2027, to December 31, 2029. This request is in response to continued volatility and rising costs within the employee benefits and insurance marketplace. Extending the agreement preserves the existing contract terms, conditions, and fixed premium rates in place since contract implementation of January 1, 2018. Maintaining these same premium rates provides important predictability for participating employees and retirees and helps protect them from potentially higher premium increases. Extending the agreement also maintains continuity of the current vision benefit structure for employees and retirees while allowing the County to continue administering a stable, predictable and competitive benefits program. There is no financial impact to the County for this program, as the cost for vision benefits are paid in full by employees and retirees. Accept HMGP Funding for Residential Home Elevations Funding: Current Year Dollar Amount: $88,000 Included in the Current Budget?: Yes Fund: Federal Grants through General Fund Comments: HMGP Grant Funded, state pass-through Item Summary: Approves a FEMA Hazard Mitigation Grant Program grant agreement through the Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM) to elevate homes that sustained significant flooding in Hurricane Ian and are located in a Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA) or are designated as a repetitive/severe loss property. The grant is limited to properties previously approved through the 2023 application process. The FEMA Elevation Program provides seventy-five percent (75%) of the funding to elevate the houses with the property owner contributing the remaining twenty-five percent (25%). The initial grant agreement provides funding for engineering, permitting, and feasibility assessments. Each property will undergo an engineering evaluation to determine whether the home can be safely elevated at a reasonable cost. Elevation projects deemed feasible may proceed to construction through future grant amendments approved by FDEM and FEMA.

Improvements may be exterior, interior or a combination of interior/exterior. Grants are contingent upon the availability of funds in the Tallahassee CRA budget. Grant awards are also contingent upon a demonstrated benefit to the CRA district and compliance with the Downtown or Greater Frenchtown/Southside Redevelopment Plan. Additional eligibility requirements and program features are described below.
